title: Deep offline inference from three RF placements
goal: Attempt room-relevant echo inference from saved complex samples by correcting nuisance response and combining overlapping frequency windows.
ground_truth: Deterministic pilot samples; physical locations and wall geometry remain unknown. Synthetic controls include specified mirror distortion, null signals, arbitrary per-window timing/phase/gain and known 35/85 ns echoes.
protocol: Recompute selected channels from hashed original IQ and compare independent capture halves.
Identify the known waveform mirror component using held-out bins.
Fit a shared smooth baseband response on spot 1 forward only; apply unchanged to all sweeps.
Reconstruct overlapping complex windows and test repeatability, model order, subcapture consistency and phase gauge sensitivity.
Compare differential responses across placements to cancel common instrument response where justified.
success_criteria: Retain raw/source provenance and all failed analysis attempts.
Recover specified synthetic echoes and avoid large false image components in null controls.
Only interpret physical echoes that survive independent repeats and nuisance-model sensitivity.
uncertainties: Unknown common radio and antenna response.
Unknown per-window phase/timing/gain, and a common quadratic phase ambiguity.
Unknown placement geometry and operator state.
failures: Initial reconstruction grid coverage failure; boundary rounding alone did not resolve the final notch hole. Both failed attempts retained; blending extent corrected without extrapolating beyond captured pilot support.
raw_data_policy: No original data are overwritten. Derived complex reconstructions are saved locally with source and output hashes.
hypothesis: Known-pilot mirror correction and approximate common fractional timing permit repeatable overlap reconstruction; interpretable echoes must survive independent repeats and nuisance-model sensitivity.
environment: Offline analysis on the Windows capture host. Original three indoor placements and orientation uncertainties are inherited unchanged.
rf_chain: Original single Pluto and supplied TX/RX antennas; no hardware access or additional RF in this pass.
calibration_state: Shared baseband curvature estimated on position 1 forward only. Absolute propagation delay, bearing, radio response and geometry remain uncalibrated.
authorization_and_limits: User explicitly requested a deeper pass on saved data. All operations used local files; no SDR connection or RF transmission.

results.short_delay_hypothesis: A roughly 5-8 ns term fits the change from spot 1 under restricted smooth-background models. A smooth cubic complex-log response with no explicit echo term predicts comparably; the delay is not identified independently of that model.

echo_injection.qualification: Known-truth algorithm sensitivity, not a calibrated detection limit.

failures_and_revisions: Two grid-coverage failures retained before fixing notch coverage with real LO rounding.
Unrestricted per-window timing amplifies slope noise; its unstable reconstructions remain as a sensitivity result.
Initial injection display shortlist excluded the central 12 ns; injection-v2 instead tests actual short-delay secondary maxima and confirms the same 16/24 resolution result.
Known-truth-v2 widens the analytic truth grid at the endpoints; original controls are retained. Explicit immutable-input bindings were added in separate provenance supplements.
The candidate short-delay interpretation is not unique: smooth cubic complex-log models predict comparably, so no room geometry is assigned.
remedies: Use the tested common-timing model for descriptive effective-channel reconstruction; retain independent repeats, shared calibration assumptions, window/model sensitivity and known-truth controls. Preserve uncertain geometry rather than invent coordinates.
